questions.q: How does Google earn almost all of its revenue?
a: Through advertising
Through hardware sales
Through cloud subscriptions
Through software licensing
questions.why: The first lesson says advertising accounts for about 95 percent of Google's revenue, so users pay with time and attention.

questions.q: Why is privacy at odds with Google's business model?
a: The model depends on collecting as much information as possible
Its founders promised to sell user data to advertisers
Its servers are unable to encrypt personal files
Its advertisers insist on reading private messages
questions.why: The summary says Google wants access to all information to build its database, so any privacy runs contrary to its model.

questions.q: How does blockchain keep bitcoin records secure?
a: Each block logs transfers and links into a chronological chain
A central bank verifies every single transaction
Only miners are allowed to see the full ledger
Passwords are stored safely on one protected server
questions.why: The second lesson describes blocks linked in order, each recording recent activity, making a bitcoin's path traceable and secure.

questions.q: What flaw does the summary find in bitcoin as a new gold standard?
a: Its fixed supply makes it too volatile as a token of exchange
Its supply grows too quickly to hold any value
It is controlled by one anonymous company
It requires more electricity than any other currency
questions.why: The third lesson says bitcoin cannot react to demand because its supply is capped at 21 million, so its value swings wildly.
